subject.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)

question: Should a successful no-op compaction permanently count as a public `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` matched pair, with `compactedCount: 0` and an informational `reason`?
rationale: The runtime fix is sound, but existing public documentation does not define no-op completion semantics, and third-party plugins may currently treat `after_compaction` as proof of a real transcript rewrite; automation cannot choose that permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Adopt Matched-Pair Semantics
options.body: Define every successful attempt as a completed lifecycle pair, document `compactedCount: 0`, clarify reason stability, then refresh and merge the branch.

options.title: Keep Real-Compaction Semantics
options.body: Preserve `after_compaction` for actual transcript changes and introduce a separate internal or typed completion/no-op signal for observers that need balancing.

options.title: Split The Validator Fix
options.body: Land the JSON-safe validator and fallback work separately while deferring the hook-contract change for focused API review.

recommendation.title: Adopt Matched-Pair Semantics
recommendation.body: Define every successful attempt as a completed lifecycle pair, document `compactedCount: 0`, clarify reason stability, then refresh and merge the branch.

likelyOwner.reason: He recently reviewed and merged compaction-hook lifecycle changes and has adjacent context-engine history, making him the best available owner for this contract choice.
